## F05.os-sandbox — OS or container sandbox

Definition: The isolation mechanism around commands or the whole agent.

Separately, the SDK can run inside a sandboxed container for process isolation, resource limits, network control, and an ephemeral filesystem. | limit: Sandboxing applies only to Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor commands and their child processes; `/sandbox` is available on supported platforms only. | ev: E-claude-code-00126, E-claude-code-12218, E-claude-code-00392, E-claude-code-07306

## F05.fs-write-scope — Filesystem write scope

Definition: Where the agent may write.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] The sandbox runtime uses OS primitives (`bubblewrap` on Linux, `sandbox-exec` on macOS) to restrict read/write access to configured paths; `allowWrite` lists file path patterns to allow write access to (default empty). Sandboxing restricts filesystem and network access, letting Claude work more freely within defined boundaries. | ev: E-claude-code-00767, E-claude-code-01453, E-claude-code-02202
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Codex CLI and the IDE extension default to write permissions limited to the active workspace. To grant write access to more directories, the docs prefer --add-dir rather than forcing --sandbox danger-full-access. The SDK Sandbox.read_only preset reads files without allowing writes. | ev: E-codex-cli-00097, E-codex-cli-01169, E-codex-cli-00382
- copilot-cli [partial, verified] By default, sandboxed commands and tools can write within the current working directory and temporary folders; the home directory, system and tool locations are read-only, and other disk locations are blocked. Copilot is granted read/write permission to everything in and below the current working directory. | limit: Built-in file-reading and file-editing tools run as part of Copilot CLI itself rather than as a sandboxed child process; the OS sandbox never sees these operations and cannot constrain them, so the tools honor the sandbox policy on a best-effort basis. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00342, E-copilot-cli-00326, E-copilot-cli-00194, E-copilot-cli-00294
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] Built-in agent tools can only read and write files within the current workspace folder, with optional read-only access to additional folders via `chat.additionalReadAccessFolders`. ## F05.network-policy — Network policy

Definition: Allowed hosts, proxies and offline modes.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] Managed sandboxing provides OS-level network isolation with domain allowlists (`sandbox.network.allowedDomains`). For production, outbound traffic can be routed through an egress proxy that enforces domain allowlists, injects credentials, and logs requests. `SandboxSettings` lets the SDK configure network restrictions programmatically. | ev: E-claude-code-00126, E-claude-code-00397, E-claude-code-00726
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Outbound network access inside the sandbox defaults to false; network_access opts in. The network_proxy feature enforces the approved domain. For the same domain rule, an admin environment override can allow a domain denied in Global or deny a domain allowed in Global; without one, the Global rule is inherited. | ev: E-codex-cli-00972, E-codex-cli-00411, E-codex-cli-01452, E-codex-cli-01111
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] The local sandbox lets outbound internet access and local network access be allowed or blocked independently; Allow outbound connections is turned on by default and turning it off fully isolates the sandbox from the network. COPILOT_OFFLINE=true runs Copilot CLI without contacting GitHub's servers. Permanently approved URL domains are added to allowedUrls in settings.json. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00297, E-copilot-cli-00331, E-copilot-cli-00472, E-copilot-cli-00491
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` (Preview) permits unrestricted network access while preserving file system restrictions; when `false`, the Copilot Agent Host built-in shell and Windows terminal sandbox block outbound access. - cursor [partial, verified] Network egress controls restrict outbound traffic to a default set plus an allowlist, or to the allowlist only; enterprise admins can lock the policy org-wide. Definition: Whether child processes inherit the restrictions.
- claude-code [partial, verified] Sandboxing's OS-level enforcement applies to Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor commands and their child processes. | limit: Claude Code runs hooks, MCP servers, and the processes a mod starts outside the sandbox; the mod network policy doesn't cover a program started with `$.process.run`. | ev: E-claude-code-12218, E-claude-code-12582, E-claude-code-12464

- copilot-cli [partial, verified] Shell commands and built-in searches run as sandboxed child processes, so the operating system enforces the policy directly. Local MCP servers and language servers can also run inside the sandbox; the Sandbox MCP servers setting is turned on by default. Copilot CLI runs most of the commands and tools it invokes inside an operating-system sandbox. | limit: Remote MCP servers are never sandboxed. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00192, E-copilot-cli-00298, E-copilot-cli-00321, E-copilot-cli-00418
- copilot-vscode [supported, verified] Sandboxing applies to terminal commands and their child processes, not to built-in file tools or other agent tools. - gemini-cli [supported, unverified] Tool-level sandboxing provides granular isolation for individual tool executions, isolating individual tools instead of the entire CLI process. ## F05.sandbox-override — Sandbox override

Definition: How a command runs outside the sandbox, and who may allow it.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] `excludedCommands` entries (for example `docker *`, default empty) bypass sandbox restrictions and run unsandboxed automatically without model involvement. Setting `failIfUnavailable` to `false` falls back to unsandboxed execution with a warning on stderr when the sandbox can't start. Commands typed at the `!` shell-mode prompt run unsandboxed in most sessions. | ev: E-claude-code-00729, E-claude-code-01433, E-claude-code-12847, E-claude-code-11092
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Where policy permits full sandbox escalation and it is approved, that execution can bypass the command proxy. thread/shellCommand runs a user-initiated shell command outside the sandbox with full access and doesn't inherit the thread sandbox policy. Sandboxing can be disabled entirely; use only if your environment already isolates processes. | ev: E-codex-cli-00106, E-codex-cli-00218, E-codex-cli-00414
- copilot-cli [partial, verified] Sandboxed commands can request a bypass for specific operations (a permission prompt is displayed). If the effective policy permits sandbox bypass, a user can explicitly disable sandboxing for the rest of the current session, from an active bypass prompt or with /sandbox disable. The --no-sandbox option disables it for this session only. | limit: If enterprise managed settings require sandboxing, ordinary configuration and the --no-sandbox command line option cannot disable it; --no-sandbox is ignored if an enterprise-managed policy enforces sandboxing and is only available in experimental mode. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00212, E-copilot-cli-01245, E-copilot-cli-00341, E-copilot-cli-00986
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] If a command cannot run inside the sandbox, the agent can ask for confirmation to run it outside; `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands` (Preview) controls this for Local and Copilot Agent Host sessions. When `false`, Allow Outside Sandbox is not offered and such requests fail. `sandbox.allowBypass` set `false` from any channel takes precedence over `true` from another. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00767, E-copilot-vscode-00581, E-copilot-vscode-00768, E-copilot-vscode-01044
- cursor [supported, unverified] If a sandboxed command fails on a sandbox restriction, such as a permission error, the agent can rerun it outside the sandbox, and the classifier reviews that rerun.
